name: Eolian
ownership: private — portfolio company of Global Infrastructure Partners ('part of BlackRock' since Oct 2024), with meaningful employee equity ('employee-owned with funds managed by GIP' per Jul 2026 PR); lineage: GIP Fund IV acquired MAP Energy's renewables business (MAP RE/ES) Dec 29, 2020 with >$2.5B equity secured; took over the Able Grid storage JV portfolios (>10 GW) Dec 2021. BlackRock's infrastructure arm also owns Jupiter Power — sponsor siblings
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Eolian is simultaneously the hardest US account for a Chinese vendor and the best case study of the energy-plus-load thesis Hithium's US market depends on. The hard part: Eolian publicly campaigns for American-built storage — a US Energy Storage Coalition member alongside Tesla, LG Energy Solution Vertech, Fluence and Form Energy, with CEO Aaron Zubaty on record (Mar 2026) that 'our American factories [are] now capable of fully supplying the systems we need' — its supplier progression runs Sungrow (Chisholm, 2021, NMC) → Wärtsilä (Madero/Ignacio, 2023) → Tesla (the entire 400 MW/1.8 GWh Padua complex), it invented standalone-storage ITC monetization (the Feb 2023 Churchill Stateside tax-equity first), and it has zero Hithium contact. The thesis part: the CyrusOne DFW7 deal (Jan 2026) monetizes Chisholm's existing interconnection to fast-track a 200 MW Fort Worth data-center campus, and Flint Grid — 200 MW/1.06 GWh, PJM's largest battery, under construction since Jul 2026 in the AWS/Meta/Google/Intel corridor near Columbus — cleared the PJM 2027/28 capacity auction at the price cap. Flint's system supplier is unannounced, as is its equal-size Phase 2 (~2029).
ecosystemRole: We assess Eolian as the ideological anchor of the domestic-storage coalition and the pioneer of turning batteries into data-center on-ramps: 'energy-plus-load' converts a BESS interconnection into speed-to-power for a hyperscale campus (CyrusOne DFW7 is the first marquee ERCOT example), and Flint demonstrates the buildable version — a 5.3-hour, GWh-class battery sited where AI load is exploding and sold through capacity markets with hyperscaler offtakes anticipated. For the relationship web: Eolian's Padua complex is Tesla's largest Texas showcase; its Oregon builds delivered assets into PGE/NextEra structures; its Prospect Power origination (sold to Swift Current, now Elevate) seeded PJM's largest operating-class BESS in Data Center Alley; and its sibling relationship with Jupiter Power under BlackRock means sponsor-level procurement norms could converge — in the American-built direction Eolian advocates.

productsAndServices.name: Owned/operating BESS fleet (ERCOT + PJM + delivered OR)
productsAndServices.description: Madero & Ignacio Grid (Mission, TX — 200 MW/>500 MWh combined ~2.5-hr, COD Mar 2023; world's largest fully-merchant BESS at COD; Wärtsilä GridSolv Quantum + GEMS with a Service+ GAP agreement; dispatch via Eolian's own software); Chisholm Grid (Fort Worth — 100 MW/125 MWh, COD 2021, Sungrow NMC, Mortenson EPC; now being modernized and repurposed to enable the CyrusOne DFW7 campus); Padua Grid Storage Complex (Bexar Co. — Padua 1: 50 MW/100 MWh COD Sep 30, 2025; Padua 2: 150 MW/600 MWh, Winter 2026; Padua 3/'Ferdinand': 200 MW/800 MWh, Spring 2026 — full complex 400 MW/1.8 GWh, largest BESS site in Texas, >$700M, ALL Tesla Megapack, CPS Energy storage-capacity agreements); Sundial Grid (Troutdale OR — 200 MW/4-hr, COD Dec 2024, operated by NextEra under a 20-yr PGE agreement) and Seaside Grid (N. Portland — 200 MW/4-hr, COD Jul 2025, delivered to PGE under a fixed-cost build-transfer agreement).
productsAndServices.positioning: Longest-duration merchant assets in ERCOT (Madero/Ignacio at COD; Padua ~4-5-hr) — competing on duration, siting and structure rather than fleet MW; Madero Grid 1 was ERCOT's top-earning battery in June 2024 at >2× the BESS index (non-spin-heavy strategy, per Modo).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant + municipal-utility capacity agreements (CPS Energy), build-transfer (PGE), long-hold GIP capital (30+ yr horizon; 'owner-operator, not build-and-flip' — though it has sold: Gambit-era heritage, Prospect Power).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: ERCOT energy/AS; muni utilities; Pacific Northwest utilities.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Chisholm modernization/upgrade retrofit (2026) is a visible procurement scope; ERCOT 2025 revenue compression (~$29.4/kW, one-sixth of 2023 per Modo) pressures merchant economics.

productsAndServices.name: Flint Grid & the PJM/data-center corridor play
productsAndServices.description: Flint Grid, Jersey Township, Licking Co. OH — 200 MW/1.06 GWh (5.3-hr) Phase 1, under construction since Jul 29, 2026, on Eolian's own balance sheet; first grid-scale BESS permitted by the Ohio Power Siting Board; largest BESS built in PJM; largest battery to clear the PJM 2027/28 Residual Capacity Auction (Dec 2025, at the maximum allowable price — >50% of all new battery capacity in that capacity year); Phase 1 online ~Jun 2027, Phase 2 of equal size planned by 2029. Sited in 'America's fastest-growing data center and industrial corridor': adjacent AWS (operating), Meta and Google (under construction), Intel's $28B fab; AEP substation interconnection; corporate/hyperscaler offtakes anticipated. In development since 2018.
productsAndServices.positioning: The proof asset for storage-as-AIDC-enabler in PJM — capacity that 'allows more stuff to get built' in a load-constrained zone.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: PJM capacity revenue + merchant + anticipated hyperscaler offtakes; balance-sheet financed (no project financing disclosed).
productsAndServices.roadmap: SYSTEM SUPPLIER UNANNOUNCED for both phases — the most valuable open procurement question on the account (though the American-built posture points at Tesla/LGES-class suppliers).

productsAndServices.name: Energy-plus-load (interconnection monetization)
productsAndServices.description: The CyrusOne DFW7 partnership (announced Jan 13, 2026): a 200 MW data-center campus co-located at Chisholm Grid — Eolian monetizes the existing high-voltage interconnection/substation ('speed to power'), modernizes the BESS, and the battery supplies initial campus phases with capacity delivery from 2026. Eolian states multiple additional energy-plus-load sites are in development across data-center markets. Origin story: Prospect Power (150 MW/600 MWh, Rockingham Co. VA) was originated ~2017-18 explicitly to serve NoVa Data Center Alley ('anywhere within 100 miles of northern Virginia' — Zubaty), sold to Swift Current 2023 ($242M financing 2025), acquired by Elevate Jan 2026, COD mid-2026 as PJM's largest standalone BESS.
productsAndServices.positioning: First-mover in converting BESS grid positions into data-center currency — the interconnection queue is the scarce asset, and Eolian holds early-vintage positions.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data-center developers needing 2026-28 power in queue-constrained markets.
productsAndServices.roadmap: CDO Eric Stoutenburg's mandate explicitly includes 'powered industrial sites' — the land-plus-power product.

productsAndServices.name: Financing innovation & royalty platform
productsAndServices.description: Invented the renewable-energy royalty structure (MAP heritage; royalty interests span 19 GW of operating wind/solar per GIP). First-ever standalone-storage ITC monetization (Feb 13, 2023, Madero/Ignacio — tax-equity fund managed by Churchill Stateside; note: structured as tax equity, not a plain §6418 transfer, and no JPMorgan-Eolian deal exists in the record). Debt spine: $100M Natixis (2021), $925M (Apr 2022, Santander/MUFG), $515M Green Loan (Jun 2023), $463M Natixis-arranged construction+term+LC for Padua 2&3 (single closing, Oct 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: The financing-innovation brand of the standalone tier — repeatable bank club (Natixis anchor; Santander, MUFG, SMBC, NAB) plus GIP's 30-year capital.
productsAndServices.roadmap: ITC-monetization dependence makes FEOC-compliant supply structurally mandatory for 2026+ vintages.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Eolian as ideologically closed to a §154-named Chinese OEM: the CEO's public identity, coalition membership with Tesla/LGES/Fluence, ITC-monetization-led financing, and hyperscaler-adjacent siting all point one direction — this is the account where the American-built argument is the product, not just the compliance posture. Displacement pitches would be counterproductive; monitor instead.

(High confidence) We assess the energy-plus-load model as the most important strategic idea in the batch for Hithium's market thesis: Eolian is proving that BESS interconnections are data-center currency (CyrusOne DFW7) and that GWh-class long-duration batteries get funded by capacity scarcity in AI corridors (Flint at the PJM price cap). This validates the demand wave Hithium needs — even though Eolian itself won't buy Chinese.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the open Flint supplier slots (Phase 1 delivering ~2027, Phase 2 ~2029) as effectively reserved for FEOC-clean vendors — Tesla and LG Energy Solution Vertech are the structural favorites given the coalition posture and the Padua precedent; a Hithium bid would serve mainly as price discovery for the buyer.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the BlackRock sibling dynamic (Eolian + Jupiter under one sponsor since the GIP absorption) as a convergence risk for Hithium's Jupiter account: if sponsor-level procurement norms harmonize, they harmonize toward Eolian's American-built doctrine, not toward Jupiter's quiet-buyer pragmatism.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: use Eolian as the leading indicator of the domestic-supply argument's credibility — its coalition's '100% American supply' claim, tested against actual 2026-27 domestic cell/system availability and pricing, is the single best public gauge of how much room remains for safe-harbored or FEOC-engineered Chinese content in the US market.

Padua 1 (50 MW/100 MWh, COD Sep 2025), Padua 2 (150 MW/600 MWh, Winter 2026) and Padua 3 'Ferdinand' (200 MW/800 MWh, Spring 2026) are all Tesla Megapack — the largest BESS site in Texas at >$700M, under CPS Energy storage-capacity agreements.

The relationship is embedded in Eolian's financing story: Tesla VP Mike Snyder was quoted in the $463M Natixis-arranged construction + term + LC financing for Padua 2&3 (Oct 2025). Tesla is the endpoint of Eolian's supplier progression (Sungrow 2021 → Wärtsilä 2023 → Tesla), consistent with its American-built advocacy.

The middle step of Eolian's supplier progression, after Sungrow and before the all-Tesla Padua complex.
